cards.title: Fair job ad
cards.text: Write a job ad for [ROLE] at [BUSINESS]. Include: what a normal week looks like, max 4 must-haves, pay and hours, how to apply. Plain English. Avoid language about age or gender, and flag any requirement that may not be needed. Details: [PASTE NOTES]

messages.text: Part-time cleaner, Fresh Start Cleaning, Columbus. 20 hrs/week, weekday daytime. Need: driver's license, reliable, eye for detail, can lift 25 lb. Young, energetic team. Pay: [PAY RANGE].

**Part-time Cleaner**, 20 hrs/week, weekdays
A normal week: daytime home cleans around Columbus.
Must-haves: driver's license · reliable timekeeping · eye for detail
Pay: [PAY RANGE] an hour

**Flagged:** "young, energetic team" can read as age bias. Try "friendly, supportive team".
Check: is lifting 25 lb truly needed?

slides.title: Always **put the pay** in the ad.
paras: Some US states and cities now require a pay range in job ads. Check your local rules.

caption:
How to write a fair, clear job ad with AI in one prompt

A vague job ad brings vague applicants. And phrases like "young team" can put good people off.

Copy this:

"Write a job ad for [ROLE] at [BUSINESS]. Include: what a normal week looks like, max 4 must-haves, pay and hours, how to apply. Plain English. Avoid language about age or gender, and flag any requirement that may not be needed. Details: [PASTE NOTES]"

On an invented cleaning business it wrote a clean ad and flagged two things: "young, energetic team" (can read as age bias) and whether lifting 25 lb is truly needed.

Tip: put the pay in. Some US states and cities require a pay range, so check your local rules.
